Subject: Dedicated reservation proposal and phased warm-up — EdenBridge

Hi Samantha —

Thanks for the time earlier. Attached is a compact draft that ties the reserve structure to EdenBridge's expected production milestones. High level: a three-stage capacity ladder (pilot, scale, steady) with a small guaranteed minimum for predictability and burst headroom for episodic training/sweeps.

Key asks from your side I captured: production readiness by Q1, predictable per-token economics, and control-plane isolation for regulated datasets. This offer sketches cluster sizes, minimum guaranteed GPUs, and a 90-day warm-up schedule that reduces ramp billing during the pilot.

Files attached: RBW-EdenBridge-Reserve-v3.pdf (proposal) and edenbridge-warmup-ramp.xlsx (ramp timeline + cost cadence).

Two quick options inside the doc you can jump to:
- Option Alpha (fast scale): 60x A100 equivalent, min guarantee 12 GPUs, 3-month ramp to full throughput; prioritized warm-start windows and 2% warmup credit each month.
- Option Beta (conservative): 32x A100 equivalent, min guarantee 6 GPUs, phased ramp over 6 months; lower monthly commitment with on-demand bursting.

Please flag any specific constraints procurement needs (billing cadence, PoP, PO terms) and Rajiv if you want procurement looped. I can revise the wording to make it procurement-friendly.

Next step suggestion: review internally and pick the option that maps to your Q1 KPI baseline; we'll produce an activation plan and SLA appendix for legal.

Thanks,
Camila Reyes

Camila —

Appreciate the thorough draft. Quick clarifying questions from our side before we take this to procurement: 

1) Can you confirm minimum activation windows for burst capacity? We need at least two 4-hour windows/day for scheduled heavy training.
2) Does the warm-up credit apply against committed spend or is it a separate month-by-month credit?
3) For the conservative option, what is the expected median P95 latency impact if we limit to the 6-GPU guarantee with bursting?

Procurement (cc) also wants the following in the next iteration: explicit billing cadence (monthly vs quarterly), a sample SOW wording for data handling (for our compliance team), and a DocuSign-ready signature page.

If you can get an updated deck that separates commercial terms from technical appendix that would speed review.

Thanks — Samantha
Head of ML Platforms, EdenBridge Therapeutics

Marissa / Karthik —

Looping you on Samantha's questions (below). Procurement wants the commercial bits explicit and DocuSign-ready. Technical ask: confirm burst activation windows and P95 latency for the conservative 6-GPU floor.

My proposed adjustments (please comment inline):

- Commercial / billing: show both monthly and quarterly billing rows in the appendix (include sample invoice cadence). Add a short SOW paragraph for data isolation and audit logs (we already have standard language; I'll paste it once legal signs off).
- Warm-up credits: make them a line-item credit applied to the first three invoice cycles against committed spend (e.g., 2% month 1, 1.5% month 2, 1% month 3) — keeps it simple for procurement.
- Bursting: commit to two 4-hour scheduled warm-start windows/day (guaranteed) and best-effort for ad-hoc bursts beyond that; add a clause that ad-hoc bursts during maintenance windows may be rate-limited.
- Performance for Beta (6 GPU floor): expect nominal P95 latency increase ~10–15% relative to full cluster baseline for heavy batching workloads; provide a table with expected token/sec at 1k/2k/4k sequence lengths. We should quantify with numbers from bench run 2026-08-11 (I'll attach results).

Can you produce updated commercial summary + a single-column tech appendix by EOD tomorrow? I'll assemble DocuSign envelope and hubspot notes.

Thanks — Camila

Samantha / Rajiv / procurement team —

Thanks for the quick turn. Per our internal review we've updated the proposal and split commercial terms out front as requested. Summary of the revisions: 

1) Billing cadence: both Monthly and Quarterly invoice options are shown; procurement can pick at signature. The DocuSign packet includes separate SOW clauses for monthly/quarterly billing and PO acceptance.

2) Warm-up credit: now explicit as credits against committed spend across the first three invoice cycles (Month1: 2%, Month2: 1.5%, Month3: 1%).

3) Bursting & activation windows: two guaranteed 4-hour scheduled warm-start windows per day (UTC 02:00–06:00 & 16:00–20:00 PT) plus on-demand burst up to 2x base throughput subject to maintenance windows. We added a short SLA clause to clarify rate-limiting during platform-wide maintenance.

4) Performance note for conservative floor: median P95 latency impact ~12% and throughput reduction ~18% for heavy batched evaluation; detailed numbers in the attached spreadsheet under tab "Bench-Results-20260811".

Attachments included: RBW-EdenBridge-Reserve-v3.pdf (updated commercial front-page) and edenbridge-warmup-ramp.xlsx (activation timeline, billing rows, bench results).

HubSpot: I've created the deal record and linked the DocuSign packet here: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/12345/EDB-2026-0929. DocuSign envelope is ready: https://www.docusign.com/en/link/EDB-0929-reserve

If that alignment looks good I'll prep the signature request and a short implementation runbook for the first 30 days (activation checklist, contact matrix, escalation path). Looking to get procurement's preferred billing cadence and whether they prefer a 30- or 60-day payment term.
